attrs.title: Problems we help with
attrs.lead: The notices we see most often. Meta gives a reason, but rarely the detail.

items.title: Ad account disabled for unusual activity
items.text:
The most common notice, and the vaguest. It can mean a failed payment, a sudden jump in spend, logins from new places, or a card used on several accounts. Meta rarely says which.

We look at payments, logins, spend and recent changes to find the most likely trigger, fix it, and explain it clearly in the review request.

items.title: Disabled after too many rejected ads
items.text:
Every rejected ad counts against the account. Before-and-after photos, “Are you…?” headlines and health or money claims are the usual causes, and after enough of them, the account goes.

We review every rejected ad, rewrite the ones that matter within Meta’s rules, and set up a simple checklist so new ads don’t get rejected.

items.title: Your profile or business is restricted
items.text:
Sometimes it isn’t the ad account at all. A restricted personal profile, or a business portfolio that can’t advertise, stops every ad account under it.

We map who and what is connected to your business, find the restricted part, and fix it: a review for the profile, a new admin, or business verification.

items.title: Hacked, then disabled
items.text:
Someone got into a profile, added themselves as an admin and ran ads you never approved. Meta disabled the account to stop it, and now you’re locked out too.

We secure every login first, remove unknown people, report the unauthorised spend, and only then request a review, with the evidence.

items.title: Special ad category problems
items.text:
Housing, jobs, credit and political ads have their own rules. Running them without the right category, or targeting by age or postcode, gets ads rejected and accounts restricted.

We set the right special ad category, rebuild targeting within the rules and complete any authorisation Meta asks for.

items.title: A review request already refused
items.text:
Meta often gives one review. If it’s refused, the decision can be final, so a rushed request in a panic is the most expensive mistake.

If you haven’t requested a review yet, we prepare it properly first. If it was already refused, we look at what’s still possible and plan how to keep leads coming.

attrs.html:
What happens after you contact us

First a call, then five steps. Careful, and honest about the outcome.

A call back within 24 hours

Send us the notice. A Meta specialist calls you back within one working day to go through it with you, before any work starts.

  • A real person
  • No obligation
  • Plain English

  1. With access to your business portfolio, we read every notice in Account Quality, check payments, people and logins, and look at your recent and rejected ads.

    You get: A clear picture of what Meta is likely seeing.

    • Notices in Account Quality
    • People, pages and ad accounts mapped
    • Payments and billing history
    • Recent and rejected ads

  2. We tell you the most likely cause in plain English, what needs to change, and honestly how strong your case is, including whether a review is still possible.

    You get: Written findings within 48 hours.

    • The most likely cause, and why we think so
    • A fix list in order of importance
    • Whether a review is still offered
    • An honest view of your chances

  3. We fix what Meta is likely to check: ads, landing pages, payments, security, people and verification.

    You get: Every change logged with screenshots.

    • Rejected ads rewritten within the rules
    • Payment method fixed and balance cleared
    • Two-factor login and unknown people removed
    • Business verification completed

  4. Once everything is fixed, we request a review with you, from the right place, with a short, factual explanation.

    You get: One review request, sent properly.

    • Review requested from Account Quality
    • A clear explanation of what changed
    • Evidence ready if Meta asks
    • A copy kept for your records

  5. We follow up on Meta’s reply. If the account comes back, we check it before ads restart. If not, we give you a plan to keep leads coming.

    You get: A plan either way.

    • Ads checked before they restart
    • A safe restart with lower budgets
    • A plan B if the review fails
    • Tips to avoid another restriction

What we check

Eight things Meta looks at, checked and fixed

For each one: why it matters, what we check, what we often find and what we change.

Area 1 of 8

Account Quality notices

Account Quality is where Meta shows what’s restricted and why. It’s the starting point, even when the reason is vague.

What we check

  • Every notice and its date
  • Which asset is restricted
  • Whether a review is offered
  • Earlier decisions
  • Ad, profile and business notices
  • Deadlines

What we often find

  • ! A notice nobody saw for weeks
  • ! The ad account blamed, but the profile is restricted
  • ! A review offered, but not yet used
  • ! Old warnings never resolved

What we change

  • A list of every restriction, by asset
  • The real problem found
  • A review used only when ready
  • Old warnings closed where possible

Area 2 of 8

Payments and billing

Failed payments and unusual billing are among the most common triggers for “unusual activity”.

What we check

  • Payment methods
  • Failed charges
  • Outstanding balance
  • Billing country and currency
  • Cards shared across accounts
  • Spending limits

What we often find

  • ! A card that declined twice
  • ! One card on three ad accounts
  • ! Billing country different from the business
  • ! A sudden jump in daily spend

What we change

  • One verified payment method
  • Balance cleared
  • Billing details that match the business
  • Spending limits for a safe restart

Area 3 of 8

Ads and creative

Repeated rejections build up against an account. Most come from a few rules that are easy to break by accident.

What we check

  • Rejected ads and the reasons
  • Before-and-after images
  • Personal attributes (“Are you…?”)
  • Health, money and weight claims
  • Text in images
  • Restricted products

What we often find

  • ! Nine before-and-after images
  • ! “Struggling with acne?” headlines
  • ! Claims of guaranteed results
  • ! Ads appealed again and again

What we change

  • Ads rewritten within the rules
  • Images that show the service, not the body
  • Claims removed or backed up
  • A checklist for new ads

Area 4 of 8

Landing pages

Meta reviews where your ads send people too. A page that doesn’t match the ad, or makes claims the ad doesn’t, can get ads rejected.

What we check

  • Page matches the ad
  • Claims on the page
  • Contact details and policies
  • Pop-ups and redirects
  • Page speed on phone
  • Pixel and Conversions API

What we often find

  • ! Pages with stronger claims than the ads
  • ! No contact details or privacy policy
  • ! Redirects to another domain
  • ! Pop-ups that block the page

What we change

  • Pages that match the ad
  • Claims in line with the rules
  • Contact details and privacy policy
  • No redirects or blocking pop-ups

Area 5 of 8

People and access

Every person with access is a way in. A restricted or hacked profile can stop the whole business.

What we check

  • Admins and their roles
  • Unknown people
  • Former staff and agencies
  • Two-factor login
  • Restricted profiles
  • Backup admins

What we often find

  • ! An admin nobody recognises
  • ! A former agency still with full control
  • ! Two-factor login off for everyone
  • ! One admin, and that profile is restricted

What we change

  • Only the people who need access
  • Two-factor login for every admin
  • A second admin as backup
  • Roles that match what people do

Area 6 of 8

Business verification

A verified business is easier for Meta to trust, and some actions need it.

What we check

  • Business details
  • Legal name and documents
  • Website and domain
  • Phone and email
  • Domain verification
  • Status of verification

What we often find

  • ! Verification never started
  • ! Documents in a different name
  • ! Domain not verified
  • ! Website without business details

What we change

  • Business verification completed
  • Documents that match
  • Domain verified
  • Business details on the website

Area 7 of 8

Special ad categories

Housing, jobs, credit, social issues and politics have their own rules for targeting and authorisation.

What we check

  • Whether a category applies
  • Targeting by age, gender or postcode
  • Authorisation for political ads
  • Country rules
  • Lookalike audiences
  • Ad wording

What we often find

  • ! Housing ads with no category
  • ! Age and postcode targeting on job ads
  • ! Loan ads with interest claims
  • ! Authorisation missing

What we change

  • The right category on every campaign
  • Targeting within the rules
  • Authorisation completed
  • Wording checked

Area 8 of 8

Review request and plan B

Meta often gives one review, so when and how you ask matters as much as what you fix.

What we check

  • Whether a review is offered
  • What to say
  • Evidence to have ready
  • When to ask
  • What happens if refused
  • Other channels

What we often find

  • ! A review requested in a panic, with nothing fixed
  • ! A new account opened to get around the block
  • ! No backup if Meta says no
  • ! Leads stopped completely

What we change

  • One review request, once everything is fixed
  • No new accounts to get around the block
  • Google Ads or other channels ready
  • A safe restart plan

attrs.title: What it’s like to work with us
Meta Ad Account Disabled Help questions, answered
attrs.lead: Can’t find your answer? Ask us on a free 30-minute call.

items.question: Why was my Facebook ad account disabled?
items.answer: Common reasons are payment problems, unusual activity, repeated policy violations, a restricted admin profile or security concerns. The notice gives a reason, but rarely the detail.

items.question: How do I request a review?
items.answer: From Account Quality in Meta Business Suite. Fix the likely cause first, because a refused review can be final.

items.question: My account was hacked. What should I do first?
items.answer: Secure every login with a new password and two-factor login, remove people you don’t recognise, and report the hack to Meta before requesting a review.

items.question: Should I open a new ad account?
items.answer: No. Opening new accounts to get around a restriction breaks Meta’s rules and usually gets the new account disabled too.

items.question: How long does a Meta review take?
items.answer: Often a few days, sometimes longer. Meta doesn’t publish a fixed time.

items.question: Can you guarantee my account comes back?
items.answer: No. Only Meta can restore an account. We fix what we can and help you make a clear request.
